newsitem.title: UK: Rock legends to play Montserrat aid gig in London.
newsitem.headline: Rock legends to play Montserrat aid gig in London.

text.p: Some of rock music's biggest stars will perform at a benefit concert in London on September 15 to raise money for the volcano-ravaged Caribbean island of Montserrat.
Eric Clapton, Elton John, former Beatle Paul McCartney, Sting and Dire Straits' frontman Mark Knopfler have agreed to perform for free, organisers said on Wednesday.

Beatles producer George Martin, who has a luxury home and recording studio on the island, is organising the concert at London's Royal Albert Hall and hopes to raise at least 500,000 pounds ($800,000), the Evening Standard newspaper said.
"Montserrat and its people mean a great deal to me. For two years I have seen them suffer and live in appalling conditions with enormous courage and fortitude," Martin said in a statement.

The artists will perform both solo, probably acoustically, and in duets, and will then assemble on stage for a finale. The proceeds will go "to relieve the distress of the homeless, the sick and aged and the young of Montserrat", the statement said.

Montserrat, a tiny British territory in the eastern Caribbean, has been devastated by natural disasters over the past decade. Its population has dwindled to around 5,800 from about 11,000 two years ago.
Recent volcano eruptions, the most serious on June 25, have killed about 20 residents, including Martin's maid Felina, and left hundreds homeless.

The British Geological Survey said the Soufriere Hills volcano would remain active, although without a drastic eruption, for between one and five years which local officials fear will leave the south side of the island unusable.

The British government said they were drawing up an aid package including financial assistance for those who wish to stay on the north side of Montserrat and resettlement grants for those who want to move to neighbouring islands. ($ = 0.613 British Pounds)
